description: Verify that DUT accepts a UDP datagram with Source Port = 0 (RFC 768 'Fields' MUST — "If not used, a value of zero is inserted")
approach:
[Objective]
RFC 768 says src_port = 0 is the legitimate sentinel for 'no reply expected', e.g. one-shot announcements. Receivers MUST NOT reject a datagram just because src_port is zero — that would break unidirectional UDP usage.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: UDP datagram
   • src_port = 0   ← key trigger
   • dst_port = a port DUT's upper-tester listens on

2. Observation:
   • DUT's upper-tester receives the datagram (UT-query confirms)

[Pass condition]
DUT delivers the src_port=0 UDP to upper-tester.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_wrong_receipt — DUT did not deliver the datagram (src_port=0 silently dropped)
• Fail_timeout — UT-query never arrived (test infra issue, indeterminate)

verdicts.Pass: DUT accepted the src_port=0 UDP — normal
verdicts.Fail_wrong_receipt: DUT did not receive the zero-source-port UDP
